primaryEvidence.title: Cephalopod-inspired embodied camouflage system for simultaneous evasion of artificial and human visual perception
primaryEvidence.officialAbstract: Differences in visual perception mechanisms between biological and artificial intelligence make it difficult to design camouflage that is both visually natural and effective against modern detectors. Existing adversarial approaches often create conspicuous patterns and are typically static, limiting their use in dynamic real-world scenarios. Here we present CephCam, an embodied closed-loop camouflage system that integrates environment-aware color extraction, optimization-based texture generation that jointly balances visual naturalness and detector evasion, and angle-aware display compensation for physical deployment. This system involves an eye-brain-skin framework of sensing, computation, and display, motivated by the naturally evolved cephalopod camouflage, but implemented with specialized cameras, computing modules, and OLED screens on a model vehicle. CephCam targets simultaneous evasion of both human observers and modern object detectors across diverse digital and physical environments, significantly outperforming strong baselines targeting either alone. These findings underscore shared vulnerabilities in human and artificial visual processing systems, showcasing CephCam’s potential for robust, adaptive, and embodied camouflage applications.

primaryEvidence.title: Headway switching, rather than feedforward loss alone, destabilises cooperative platoons under V2X dropout
primaryEvidence.officialAbstract: Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control (CACC) uses vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication to sustain short, string-stable headways, but real wireless links drop packets, eroding this guarantee. We show that at a representative moderate-loss point, discontinuous headway switching on packet loss, not feedforward loss itself, is the dominant destabilising mechanism: a canonical plant-inverting design remains string stable losing feedforward at fixed headway, but not when switching headway on loss. Continuous, non-learned scheduling recovers stability at moderate but not severe loss. We train a dropout-aware multi-agent reinforcement-learning (TD3) controller with a learned V2X reliability gate; four of five training seeds converge to a policy string stable at \(30\%\) and \(60\%\) loss, outperforming the strongest classical scheduler under V2X-only information. The comparison is not information-matched: the learned policy also observes an idealised, always-exact onboard predecessor acceleration no classical controller here uses, and a non-learned controller given that signal alone is competitive with it, limiting attribution to learning. Frequency sensitivity, severe-burst robustness, and training reliability are all seed-dependent. These results identify switching, not information loss, as a primary vulnerability of communication-dependent platooning, and give a candid account of how much a learning-based remedy owes to learning itself.

primaryEvidence.title: ASC-MAPPO: attention-based communication and safety-constrained multi-agent proximal policy optimization for cooperative path planning and dynamic obstacle avoidance of connected autonomous vehicles
primaryEvidence.officialAbstract: Fleets of connected autonomous vehicles have to solve two problems at once: they must agree on who goes first, and each of them must stay clear of traffic that nobody controls. This paper presents ASC-MAPPO, an attention- and safety-constrained variant of multi-agent proximal policy optimization designed for exactly that coupling. The planning task is cast as a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process and solved with centralized training and communication-enabled distributed execution. Each vehicle encodes its own observation into a 128-dimensional embedding, broadcasts it inside a 50 m radius, and aggregates the messages it receives through a masked four-head attention module that weights neighbours by situational relevance rather than treating them alike. A shared-parameter actor emits continuous steering increments and longitudinal accelerations; agent-wise critics and a monotonic mixing network resolve credit assignment during training only. Safety is enforced on two levels. A differentiable Gaussian risk surrogate shapes the reward and supplies smooth gradients, and a projection layer confines every executed action to an admissible set defined by obstacle clearance, road boundaries, lane keeping and friction-limited vehicle dynamics. Collisions themselves are always decided by a binary contact test, never by the surrogate. In CARLA experiments covering highway merging, a four-way intersection and a curved rural road, with four cooperative vehicles and three obstacle densities, ASC-MAPPO reaches a 99.2% avoidance success rate in the dedicated avoidance suite, shortens the mean fleet arrival time in the high-density intersection by 18.2% relative to MAPPO (11.6% when averaged over all scenarios and densities) and attains a cooperative efficiency of 0.93. Ablations separate the contributions of communication, attention, value decomposition and the projection layer; transfer tests, a complexity analysis and latency measurements for up to twelve vehicles delimit the operating envelope of the method.

primaryEvidence.title: Autonomous Driving Decision-Making at Unprotected Intersections Based on Right-of-Way and Attention
primaryEvidence.officialAbstract: Autonomous driving at complex unprotected intersections requires coordinated decisions among multiple vehicles, whereas single-vehicle decision-making cannot adequately exploit shared information and may reduce overall traffic efficiency. This study therefore proposes a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for cooperative decision-making among intelligent connected vehicles (ICVs) at unprotected intersections. Specifically, a Decision Data Preprocessing Based on Conflict Prediction (DPCP) module identifies trajectory conflicts and masks conflict-free vehicles before policy inference, thereby reducing decision-irrelevant observations. A distance-based first-in-first-out (FIFO) priority is incorporated into the reward function to guide an orderly passing sequence using only positional information. In addition, an asymmetric attention architecture employs Multi-Head Attention (MHA) in each decentralized actor to extract decision-relevant information and a Graph Attention Network (GAT) in the centralized critic to model global cooperative relationships. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a higher reward and average speed and a lower collision rate than IPPO, MADDPG, and MAPPO, while exhibiting robust performance under the randomized initial conditions considered in the fully connected and automated intersection setting.

primaryEvidence.title: Generative Video-LiDAR world models for long-horizon multimodal scene simulation with temporal and geometric consistency
primaryEvidence.officialAbstract: The training and evaluation of autonomous-driving perception systems rely on multimodal scene data. However, limited real-world long-tail scenarios have made generative world models an important complementary data source. Existing methods mainly focus on unimodal video generation or implicit training supervision, making test-time Camera–LiDAR conflict resolution and explicit consistency assessment difficult. This paper proposes a Video–LiDAR joint generation framework for extended-horizon scene synthesis that introduces consistency constraints into sampling and state space through three mechanisms. First, projection, depth–range consistency, and ray-visibility gradient corrections are incorporated into diffusion sampling to maintain cross-modal geometry. Second, a recoverability-based formulation compares predicted and re-encoded states to constrain temporal and identity consistency over rollout horizons up to 10 s. Third, failure-feedback-driven counterfactual interventions are designed to cover selected long-tail conditions. Experiments on Waymo and nuScenes show that, compared with the MagicDrive-V2-adapted baseline, the proposed method reduces Waymo Proj.Err. by 16.6% (Holm-adjusted p = 0.030) and Drift by 15.5%, while improving IDF1 by 1.6 points. Improvements on nuScenes are smaller and less consistent. With 30% LiDAR retention, the Long-tail mAP decline is reduced from 18.1% to 14.0%. On held-out real long-tail scenes, counterfactual augmentation improves Long-tail mAP from 34.1 to 35.5, compared with 34.6 using ordinary generated data, showing potential utility for challenging long-tail evaluation. Ablation studies reveal distinct effects of the three modules on geometry, identity, and long-tail performance. This work integrates training-stage modeling and sampling-stage correction for recoverability-based multimodal geometric and temporal consistency.
